about: Core ComfyUI has its own mesh nodes, so any graph can clean a generated mesh without a node pack. These are the ones a clean-up uses. Load a GLB with Load3DAdvanced, then Get3DComponents gives the mesh.

core.does: Joins vertices that sit on top of each other. Do this first: the other tools need a welded mesh.
Cuts faces down to a budget. The count is a ceiling, and it varied from run to run in our test.
Rebuilds the surface evenly from a distance field. Follow it with DecimateMesh for an exact budget.
Closes small, nearly flat holes. Large openings stay open.
Smooth shading, with edges sharper than the crease angle kept hard.
Makes UVs for texturing. Seam vertices are duplicated.
Turns the mesh by Euler angles or a quaternion.
Vertex and face counts and which attributes the mesh has, as text.
A picture of the mesh: texture, vertex colour, clay, normals or depth.

pictures.alt: Normals render of the Hunyuan3D sample before clean-up: 181,548 faces, rough fur-like detail.
The same view after welding, decimating to 6,612 faces and smoothing normals: smooth, with a few flipped triangles on the legs.
The cleaned mesh turned 45 degrees by RotateMesh, the angle worked out by a maths node.

proof.caption: Our test, 2 November 2026, on the Hunyuan3D sample from the shelf above: 181,548 faces in, 6,612 out for a budget of 8,000, in 2.5 s on a separate ComfyUI with no internet. The speckles on the legs are flipped triangles the decimation left. The same clean-up run twice more gave 6,547 and 6,588 faces. These pictures come from the twin of the graph below that takes the angle from ComfyMath-NG; the graph below uses core's own ComfyMathExpression. World Kit props carry a hidden collision box, and Get3DComponents merges it into the mesh, so on those RenderMesh drew the box.

packs.name: ComfyUI-GeometryPack
packs.why: It adds what core lacks: booleans, alpha wrap, self-intersection repair, skeletons and surfaces from point clouds. It loads only through its own installer, which pip-installs comfy-env and comfy-3d-viewers and then downloads a separate environment with CGAL and Blender. We did not install it, so we have not run it. GPL-3.0-or-later.

packs.name: ComfyMath-NG
packs.why: 64 maths nodes with dropdowns, Vec2/3/4 maths among them. It loaded in Pack Lab, and its value turned the mesh in the third picture. Not part of the studio's install. Apache-2.0.
